verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both inequalities are present, with the paper's weight and the paper's distance. δ matches on the nose: distance v X = min{1, log X − log X_a, log X_b − log X} = min{1, log(X/X_a), log(X_b/X)}. Domains match: X ∈ (X_a, X_b), η ∈ [−1,1]. The lower bound carries a single c > 0 with no derivative index, as the paper's “constant c > 0, independent of α”; the jet bound produces C and the exponent N per derivative order, as the paper's C_α, m_α per multi-index. Three routine rewritings. (1) Derivative indexing: Lean bounds the full n-th Fréchet derivative ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n …‖ of (η,X) ↦ T₀(X,η), the paper bounds each mixed ∂^α = ∂_X^{α₁}∂_η^{α₂}; evaluating the n-linear map on the coordinate basis vectors gives |∂^α T₀| ≤ ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ |α| T₀‖, so the Lean bound yields the paper's with C_α = C_{|α|}, m_α = N_{|α|} (and it is in that respect the stronger statement, one constant for all α of a given order). (2) Norm: `stress` lands in ℝ × ℝ, whose Mathlib norm is the max of the components, while the paper's |T₀| is the Euclidean length; the two differ by a factor at most √2, absorbed in c and C. (3) The two inequalities are two declarations rather than one display, both for the same profile v.profiles and the same zeta.
